title: Small limits of accessible set-valued functors
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, and an ordinary category $\mathcal C$ with small Hom sets. Regular means that unions of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ have size less than $\kappa$; a category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone. Let $K$ be a small category with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms, and let $H:K\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U})$ be a diagram of functors. Suppose that every $H(k)$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits that exist in $\mathcal C$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then the pointwise limit functor $L:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U}$, defined by $L(X)=\lim_{k\in K}H(k)(X)$ with its canonical projections, preserves these colimits as well. The empty indexing category is allowed.
